technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring XD module architecture (source/sink) based on Spring Integration and Spring Boot.
For the JDBC source (U1), use Spring Integration's JDBC polling channel adapter with configurable SQL query and row-to-message conversion.
For the Redis sink (U2), use Spring Data Redis RedisTemplate to write messages to a configurable Redis list or pub/sub channel.
For ZooKeeper security (U3), enable ZooKeeper ACLs with digest authentication on the connections used by Spring XD and restrict znode access accordingly.
For the Trigger abstraction (U4), refactor the existing Trigger interface to provide an abstract base class and allow custom implementations to be plugged in via module configuration.
For custom module guidance (U5), create a sample module project and accompanying documentation that follows recommended Spring XD conventions.
For the Kafka sink (U6), use the Kafka producer API (or Spring Integration Kafka) to publish messages to a configurable topic.
For the e2e test fix (U7), modify the Grunt/Protractor test harness to correctly manage the server process lifecycle within a single process and avoid the socket hang up error.
For HTTPS (U8), upgrade Spring Boot to 1.1.7 SNAPSHOT and configure SSL for the Admin server using standard server.ssl properties.
Use Gradle as the build tool to manage dependency versions and module assembly.
assumptions: A single experienced developer performs all activities; effort is expressed in workdays (8 hours per day).

The introductory description about Spring Framework 6 / Java 17 is contextual background; the actual increment targets Spring XD with Spring Boot 1.1.x as indicated by the user stories, so Java 8 is assumed.
Databases for the JDBC source are accessed via standard JDBC; no database-specific code beyond standard SQL is required.
ZooKeeper security is limited to ACL/digest authentication; no Kerberos or external IAM integration is in scope.
Local or CI test environments for Redis, Kafka, ZooKeeper, and databases are available and do not require effort to provision.
The e2e test fix (U7) requires changes only to the test harness and possibly minor server lifecycle code, not to production application logic.
Documentation is delivered as Markdown/Wiki pages consistent with the Spring XD project.
Effort estimates include writing automated unit and integration tests but exclude separate manual user acceptance testing.
All required third-party libraries (JDBC drivers, Redis client, Kafka client, etc.) are publicly available and compatible with the chosen stack.
